Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the Nexara Cloud Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, we will conduct a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad. There will be a brief pause while we poll for questions. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us. Today, we will be discussing Nexara Cloud's results for the Q2 2024. With me on the call are Sarah Chen, Chief Executive Officer; Mike Patel, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Lena Novak, Chief Technology Officer; and Raj Singh, Chief Product Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call contains forward-looking statements. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Nexara Cloud had an exceptional Q2, exceeding expectations across all key metrics. This success is a testament to our innovative technology, dedicated team, and strong customer relationships.

During the quarter, we focused on five key areas:
1. Expanding our market share in key verticals.
2. Investing in cutting-edge research and development.
3. Enhancing our cloud security posture.
4. Driving operational efficiencies.
5. Strengthening our ecosystem partnerships.

One critical element fueling this momentum has been our thoughtful pricing strategies and discounting programs, which have played a pivotal role in accelerating customer acquisition, retention, and expansion in this fiercely competitive cloud landscape. We're up against giants like AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud, but our approach has powered robust revenue growth while carefully managing margin dynamics.

In Q2, total revenue climbed 28% year-over-year to $3.7 billion, with cloud services—our primary engine—surging 32% to $3.2 billion. About 40%, or roughly $1.1 billion of that growth, stemmed directly from these pricing optimizations and selective discounts. We reduced effective pricing by around 7% portfolio-wide versus last year, through enhanced Savings Plans and innovative usage-based options. This spurred a 42% jump in consumption volumes, especially in booming segments like AI/ML workloads and container orchestration on our Nexara Orchestrator platform.

Quantifying the discounts: enterprise agreements over $10 million ARR averaged 18% off list prices, up from 15% a year ago, linked to multi-year Reserved Capacity Instances and Flexible Savings Plans that now apply to 65% of qualifying compute and storage. These incentives unlocked $850 million in additional bookings from 450 new enterprise customers, including key victories over Azure in financial services and healthcare. That said, it trimmed our dollar-based gross margin by 220 basis points to 71.8%, largely from promotional credits for pioneers adopting our Nexara AI Foundry.

Breaking it down by workload: for compute and storage, pay-as-you-go VM and Nexara ObjectStore rates stayed steady, but tiered volume breaks for over 1 PB/month drove 35% higher storage attachment, lifting revenue per petabyte 15% net of 8% list reductions. Spot instances, discounted 85% from on-demand, grabbed 22% of flexible workloads like Spark-based ETL, contributing $400 million in high-volume, lower-margin revenue.

In AI/ML, our Committed AI Capacity offering provides up to 30% savings on 1- or 3-year NVIDIA H100 GPU reservations through Nexara Accelerate—$2.50 per GPU-hour committed versus $4.20 on-demand, a 40% cut. This sealed 120 deals worth $2.2 billion in future ARR, boosting AI inference uptake 55% year-over-year, stealing share from Google TPUs and Azure OpenAI setups.

Serverless and databases saw bundled edge computing discounts propel 48% adoption growth, with serverless ARPU up 12% to $1,200 despite 5% competitive compression.

Geographically tailored: North America (65% of revenue) at 16% discounts fueled 25% growth with strong TCO focus amid tech capex caution. EMEA (18%) stayed conservative at 14% for GDPR premiums, hitting 30% growth via sovereign cloud in Germany and France with certification advantages. APAC (17%) went aggressive at 22% to break into Japan, India, and Southeast Asia, driving 45% growth—like $280 million from Indian telco migrations—but pinching margins to 68% on forex and Alibaba rivalry.

This aligns with our land-and-expand model, pushing net revenue retention to 128% as discounts expand wallet share from 25% to 32% in year one, projecting 3x lifetime returns. Ecosystem ties—like zero-egress for data-heavy apps and Kubernetes portability—cut multi-cloud churn 15%, with 70% of Savings Plan users moving to PaaS.

Amid GenAI's $200 billion capex surge, we're primed for inference economics, countering risks like Azure's deeper cuts or EU bundling rules with AI-dynamic pricing. Q3 embeds 6-8% more optimization for 30% growth at 71% margins, plus outcome-based AI pilots.

These strategies underscore our balance of growth and profitability, now I'll turn the call over to Mike Patel to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Mike Patel:
Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah highlighted, we had a stellar financial performance in the Q2. Revenue grew by 29% year-over-year to $3.7 billion, significantly outpacing industry averages. Our gross margin was 74.2%, reflecting our pricing power and efficient cost management. Our operating margin was 28%.

Let me now turn to one of our most vital metrics for revenue visibility: Remaining Performance Obligations, or RPO. This captures the value of signed contracts awaiting revenue recognition, offering a strong view into our future in this subscription-driven cloud world. We break it out into current RPO—due within 12 months—and total RPO, including longer-term portions.

Critical for our IaaS and PaaS model with 3-5 year enterprise deals, it smooths capex swings and macro pressures. Heavy on reserved instances, committed discounts, and AI elastic needs.

Q2 total RPO hit $48.2 billion, up 29% YoY and 8% QoQ—our 11th straight 25%+ YoY quarter, beating Gartner's 22% cloud market. Current RPO: $16.7 billion, +35% YoY, +12% QoQ. At 1.18x our $14.2 billion ARR, that's over 14 months of coverage.

Dollar-based net expansion rate held at 118%, with 85% from top 500 customers expanding 20-30% yearly on sticky workloads like Kubernetes PaaS ERP or Nexara GPU genAI. Non-current RPO: $31.5 billion, +27% YoY; new $10M+ ACV deals average 42 months, up from 36.

Drivers: AI/HPC boom—40% of bookings, 50% new RPO—from Fortune 50s committing $500M+ to Nexara AI for H100/H200 LLM fine-tuning, 30% lower TCO via tensor compilers. Synergy: 80% AI cloud growth.

Expansions: 62% of additions, $2.8M average—like automotive OEM scaling $150M to $450M for sims with VMware Tanzu hybrid.

New logos: $1.2B current RPO from healthcare/finance on HIPAA sovereign and FedRAMP. 95% Global 2000 coverage, e.g., European bank Oracle to Autonomous DB PaaS.

Segments: IaaS (compute/storage) $26.5B (55%), +32% YoY, AI reserves +55%. PaaS/SaaS (Analytics/Functions) $16.9B (35%), +26%, Functions +40% QoQ. Emerging (edge/IoT/sustainability) $4.8B (10%), +60% on 5G and CSRD APIs.

Regions: Americas 62% ($29.9B), +28%, U.S. public sector $800M. EMEA 24% ($11.6B), +35%, €300M German Industry 4.0. APAC 14% ($6.7B), +45%, Singapore telco $200M 5G.

Total RPO: 2.1x ARR years, resilient with 92% utilization via AI forecasting, 78% margins. Bets: Nexara Bedrock 2.0 Q4 for $5B RPO FY25; Fabric for Azure/AWS hybrid, 70% RFP wins; Scope 3 tracking for ESG.

RPO points to 25-30% growth FY25, 95%+ current conversion, $20B ARR year-end, Q3 guide $3.65-3.70B.

Now, I'll hand it over to Dr. Lena Novak for a technical update.

Dr. Lena Novak:
Thank you, Mike. From a technology perspective, we made significant strides in several key areas this quarter. We are proud to announce the general availability of our new Nexara AI Platform, which offers unparalleled performance and scalability.

Building on that, our energy efficiency and sustainability initiatives are core to our tech strategy, attracting investor focus and delivering cost savings, margin gains, and differentiation in a market where data centers could eat 8% of global power by 2030 per IEA.

Q2 fleet-wide PUE averaged 1.14 across 45 data centers, down from 1.18 YoY, beating UHGBC's 1.55 peer average—yielding 22% lower energy per exabyte, saving $285 million in power. WUE: 0.12 L/kWh, +15% via closed-loop cooling.

Backed by $4.2B multi-year roadmap: 1.2M Nexara Graviton4 ARM chips (35% better perf/watt vs x86); NexTensor TPUs cut AI inference 42% like TPU v5p; direct-to-chip liquid cooling in 65% racks drops cooling to <25% IT load.

Renewables: 92% matched (up from 78%), 15GW PPAs with Ørsted/NextEra; 100% hourly carbon-free U.S. West, offsetting 2.8M tons CO2e.

Regional: EMEA 85% local renewables, Frankfurt/Paris PUE 1.10 for CSRD wins like Siemens. Americas N. Virginia/Oregon 98% renewables, sub-1.10 PUE. APAC efficiency-first, 28% peak cut, 1.2GW Japan RE100 geothermal/solar.

Software: Nexara Optimizer RL-migrates workloads, -37% idle; Sustainable Compute tier +150% QoQ, $450M ARR; Functions 55% lower energy/tx.

Boosted non-GAAP gross to 72.1%, +210bps, power 4.2% revenue. FY25 $1.1B capex for immersion cooling PUE<1.05, 15-20% annual savings vs 180% AI growth.

Gartner: 68% RFPs factor sustainability; our 45% lower carbon/workload wins. NVIDIA/Equinix ties for AI edge.

Net-zero 2035, tracked publicly—this flywheel scales us sustainably.

I'll now pass it to Raj Singh for a product roadmap update.

Raj Singh:
Thank you, Dr. Novak. This quarter, we launched Nexara Bedrock 2.0, a game-changing solution for enterprise AI markets. Early customer feedback has been overwhelmingly positive. We are seeing strong demand and a rapid increase in adoption.

Central to this success is our sharpened focus on new customer acquisition costs, or CAC, a key gauge of our go-to-market efficiency amid intensifying rivalry for AI/ML, analytics, and hybrid cloud workloads. We calculate CAC as sales/marketing spend—including commissions, programs, partners, demand gen—over New ARR from quarterly sign-ups.

Q2 blended CAC: $238/$New ARR, -15% YoY from $280, -4% QoQ from $248—seventh straight compression via product-led growth and partners. Aligns with Snowflake ~$250, below Datadog <$230, legacy $350+.

By segment: Enterprise (>$1M ARR, 62% New ARR) $312, -12% YoY; 9-12mo cycles, +18% win rates via Cloud Migration Accelerator (40% faster PoVs), e.g., $15M Fortune 50 SAP HANA.

Mid-market ($100K-$1M) $189, -22% YoY; inbound SEO on multi-cloud cost tools, 28% MQL wins.

SMB (<$100K) $112, -28% YoY; freemium serverless drew 45K sign-ups.

Payback: 14.2 months, from 17.1; NRR 128%, LTV:CAC 4.8x >3x threshold.

S&M/New ARR: 28% vs 35%; digital/ABM 42% new logos (+12%), AI lead scoring +35% conv, -22% media/lead; partners (Accenture/Deloitte) 31% New ARR (+7%), 2.5x ROI; marketplaces cut enterprise CAC 18%.

Regions: Americas 72% New ARR, $215 (-17% YoY), FedRAMP wins. EMEA 18%, $265 (-11%), Dublin sovereign. APAC 10%, $298 (-9%), Singapore/China pilots.

Flywheel: low CAC funds AI/edge innovation; Rule of 40 at 48%. Q3 $230-240 CAC, payback <14mo.

This sets us for 25%+ ARR growth FY25 vs subsidized rivals.

Now, back to Sarah Chen.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Raj. We are incredibly excited about the future. We believe our investments in innovation, our commitment to customer success, and our talented team will continue to drive strong growth and value creation.

Rounding out our financial story, let's examine our cloud services gross margin, a cornerstone of profitability at 74.2% for Q2—up 320bps YoY from 71.0%, +110bps QoQ from 73.1%. Eleventh straight expansion quarter, ahead of ~72% industry (AWS 74.5%, Azure 72.8%), via mix shifts, efficiencies, capacity discipline.

Cloud revenue (92% total, $3.4B): IaaS/PaaS/SaaS minus data center/power/bandwidth/support COGS.

1. Mix to high-margin (+450bps): AI/ML/analytics $1.1B (+58% YoY, 15% mix vs 9%); >82% margins vs 68% basic compute. Nexara AI Platform LLM inference +120% QoQ on NexTensor Cores (40% better TOPS/watt H100). Serverless Functions 78% margins, legacy storage/VMs -3% mix.

2. Efficiencies/utilization (+280bps): 86% utilization (vs 82%), Nexara Orchestrator RL predicts 95%; idle -22%. Graviton4 55% fleet (vs 35%), 35% lower power, 25% perf/watt, dep/rack -18% on $2.1B capex. Software JIT/patching -5% opex.

3. Regional/pricing (+150bps): NA 65% rev 78.5%, PUE 1.12. APAC 73.2%, Japan/Singapore sovereign. EMEA 68.4% on energy (+25%), countered by 2GW PPAs. 4-6% hikes low-util reserves, 98% retention.

Headwinds (-200bps): power +12%, GPU premiums; PaaS comp press 72% basic DB. Mitigated by Nexara Guardrails auto-scale, 30% customer savings, higher util.

Outlook: +200-300bps FY25 to 76-77% on AI 25% rev, Graviton5 50% gains, edge 5G. Capex peaks 12% rev ($4.2B) then 10%, 90% util. Risks: energy vol, EU power caps; $5B sustain fund.

Scale (1.2M servers YTD) + execution for 25%+ op margins in $200B+ 22% growing market.

With that, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, if you would like to register for a question, please press star one on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from Ben Thompson with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Ben Thompson:
Thanks, and congrats on a strong quarter. On RPO, can you expand on the AI contribution and how it factors into multi-year visibility amid GPU constraints?

Sarah Chen:
Thanks, Ben. Absolutely, AI drove over 40% of Q2 bookings and half of new RPO additions, with major commitments like Fortune 50 retailers at $500M+ for our Nexara AI Platform using H100/H200 clusters. These multi-year deals, averaging 42 months for large ACV, lock in capacity against shortages, bolstered by our 30% TCO edge via tensor compilers. Combined with expansions from top customers, this gives us 2.1 years of ARR backlog, de-risking growth to 25-30% through FY25.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
Great, thanks. Mike, on CAC, what gives you confidence in continued compression into Q3, especially in APAC?

Mike Patel:
Hi Lisa, good question. Our seventh straight quarter of declines to $238 reflects product-led maturity and partner leverage—42% digital new logos, AI scoring boosting conversions 35%. APAC at $298 improved 9% YoY via Singapore scaling and China pilots; nascent but fast paybacks. With NRR at 128% and LTV:CAC 4.8x, we see Q3 at $230-240, payback under 14 months, supporting Rule of 40 at 48%.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Rivera with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Tom Rivera:
Thanks, team. Lena, sustainability—how are PUE gains translating to competitive wins, particularly EMEA?

Dr. Lena Novak:
Thanks, Tom. Our 1.14 PUE saved $285M, directly aiding 72.1% gross margins. In EMEA, 85% local renewables and 1.10 PUE in Frankfurt/Paris secured shifts from ESG buyers like Siemens/Unilever, 20-30% workloads. Gartner says 68% RFPs prioritize this; our 45% lower carbon footprint, plus NVIDIA/Equinix ties, positions us for AI infra leadership, targeting PUE<1.05 FY25.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you for your insightful questions and your continued interest in Nexara Cloud. We remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the call.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
